rule: Top warm-up bar speed >= 5% above the 6-week median -> offer +2.5% on the main lift if warm-ups feel crisp
summary: VBT and RIR-based autoregulation give strength gains similar to or slightly better than fixed percentages, supporting daily velocity-informed loading in principle. But 5% sits inside typical device and day-to-day error for mean velocity (typical error up to ~9%, SWC 1.7-7.4% for a linear transducer; phone/camera apps likely worse), so this will often fire on noise. It is only an optional +2.5% offer gated by feel, so the cost is small; consider aligning with the 10% slow threshold if it fires often.

sources.note: Meta-analysis: autoregulated loading (RPE or velocity) gave similar 1RM gains to percentage-based loading
Trained men: velocity-dictated loads matched or beat percentage-based strength gains with less volume
Linear transducer velocity typical error 0.6-8.8%, SWC 1.7-7.4% - a 5% change may be noise
Velocity tracks %1RM very closely (R2 0.98 bench), so a real velocity rise implies more capacity that day
